newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money steady in liquid market.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money steady in liquid market.

text.p: * Overnight rates hit high of 10.75 pct
Manila overnight rates averaged 10.53125 percent for the 12th straight trading session on Wednesday as cash from maturing fixed and floating rate notes swamped the system, traders said.
"Banks have enough money because of a net inflow of six billion pesos from the maturity of floating rate treasury notes since Monday," said one dealer.
Traders also said investors were reluctant to park their excess cash in reverse repos due to the 20 percent tax imposed recently by the government.
The rates hit a high of 10.75 percent in midsession, with volume dwindling to 5.559 billion pesos from 5.665 billion. Lenders outpaced borrowers 22 to 12.

In the secondary market for government securities, sellers for short-term bills dominated trading. Dealers said a number of banks are selling their treasury bill inventories in the belief that interest rates have already hit bottom.

A Reuter survey of six banks showed three-month bills were being bid at 10.70 to 10.75 percent and offered at 10.60 to 10.675 percent; six-month bills were being bidded at 10.85 to 11.125 percent and offered at 10.65 to 11 percent; and, one-year bills were bidded at 11.40 to 11.55 percent and offered at 11.3 to 11.375 percent.
